text:
The Avalanche were down 2-0 at the United Center before the game was eight minutes old, and they never trailed again once Nazem Kadri and Jaden Schwartz scored 26 seconds apart late in the first. Wyatt Kaiser's opener, a wrist shot we gave a 2% chance of going in, and Roman Kantserov's snap shot had Chicago ahead. Kadri, drafted seventh overall by Toronto in 2009, and Schwartz, the 14th pick in 2010, each finished with two goals in a 5-2 COL win. T.J. Hughes, an undrafted free agent out of Michigan, added two assists.

The score matches how the game was played. By expected goals, which measure the quality of chances, COL won the first period 2.25 to 0.43, and the Blackhawks' early lead owed more to a lucky bounce than to pressure. Our simulations give COL a 71% chance of winning a replay of this game (what we call deserved to win). The second period was even at 1.05 apiece, and Kadri's power-play tip-in and Schwartz's goal with 11 seconds left in the period turned an even stretch into a two-goal cushion. Chicago's goalie Spencer Knight allowed 4 goals against 3.42 expected, while Mackenzie Blackwood stopped 21 of 23 for COL. Connor Bedard had four shots and an assist but was on the ice for slightly more expected goals against than for.

The Avalanche have now won three straight, and the way they erased a two-goal deficit without panic is the kind of response we'd watch as the schedule gets heavier. The Blackhawks showed they can score first and still let a game get away.
